artists.biography:
Simple Minds are a Scottish rock band who achieved worldwide popularity from the mid-1980s to the early 1990s. 
The band produced a number of critically acclaimed albums in the early 1980s and best known for their No. 1 US, Canada and Netherlands hit single "Don't You (Forget About Me)", from the soundtrack of the John Hughes film The Breakfast Club. They are also known for the No. 3 US hit single "Alive and Kicking" and the No. 1 UK hit single "Belfast Child". The band has sold more than 60 million albums since 1979. 
The core of the band is the two remaining founder members - Jim Kerr (vocals, songwriting) and Charlie Burchill (guitars, keyboards after 1990, other instruments, songwriting) - and drummer Mel Gaynor (who first joined the band in 1982). The other current band members are Andy Gillespie (keyboards) and Ged Grimes (bass guitar). Significant former members include bass guitarist Derek Forbes and keyboard player Michael MacNeil (the latter credited as a significant band composer during the band's rise in the 1980s).

perplexity.description:
Released in October 1985 on Virgin Records, Once Upon a Time is the seventh studio album by Scottish band Simple Minds and stands as a landmark in their discography. Musically, the album blends electronic textures with anthemic rock, characterized by expansive production, layered synthesizers, and powerful vocals. Produced by Jimmy Iovine and Bob Clearmountain, the record features a polished, arena-ready sound that helped define the mid-1980s rock landscape. The album’s style fuses the band’s post-punk roots with a more accessible, radio-friendly approach, resulting in a collection of dramatic, emotionally charged tracks.

Once Upon a Time marked Simple Minds’ commercial breakthrough, reaching number one in the UK and the Netherlands, and the top ten in the US. It spawned four major hit singles—“Alive and Kicking,” “All the Things She Said,” “Sanctify Yourself,” and “Ghost Dancing”—and became their most successful album to date, selling over two million copies within two months. The album’s critical reception was strong, praised for its ambition and sonic grandeur, and it cemented Simple Minds’ status as international rock stars. With its iconic artwork by Anton Corbijn and a sound that bridged electronic experimentation and mainstream rock, Once Upon a Time remains a quintessential album of the era.
